input.text: The Krebs cycle, also known as the citric acid cycle, is a series of chemical reactions used by all aerobic organisms to release stored energy through the oxidation of acetyl-CoA derived from carbohydrates, fats, and proteins. Each cycle produces 2 CO2 molecules, 1 GTP, 3 NADH, and 1 FADH2. It takes place in the mitochondrial matrix.
